pageCache.text:
Welcome to Milbourne Lodge School
Located in stunning grounds near to Esher, we provide a private Pre-Prep and Prep school education for children aged between 4 and 13 years. At Milbourne Lodge we value every child, and create lasting memories, and our personalised focus and inspirational teaching is reflected in our outstanding academic results. We are united in a passion to maximise the potential and development of each child.
Nurturing Excellence
Our aim is to develop every child so that they can reach their full potential. We know that there is far more to education than academic achievement and the school provides an environment where all talents can be nurtured and celebrated. We are proud of our long history of success at securing Scholarship and Senior entry to the top Day and Boarding schools in the country.
Inspiring Futures
We are extremely proud of our ability to prepare your child for his or her next school. We are committed to guiding and supporting each child to develop their independent and critical thinking skills, to nurture their curiosity and to have the confidence to be the very best version of themselves, eager to take the next steps.
Meet our Head
Having had my own children educated at Milbourne Lodge, I have a deep understanding of what makes this school so special: It is our unique history and heritage and our strong sense of community. The depth and breadth of our unique curriculum, combined with the passion, creativity and dedication of my staff ensures that we fulfil each child's potential. We send boys and girls to a range of prestigious institutions but, most importantly, we create long and lasting memories of the joy of learning and build independence of thought and resilience of spirit, laying down strong foundations for their future. Judy Waite, Head
Tatler Schools Guide 2026
We are delighted to have been named in the Tatler Schools Guide 'Top Prep and Public Schools in the UK'.
Independent Prep of the Year
We are delighted to have been shortlisted for Independent Prep School of the Year 2025. This nomination is a testament to the passion and dedication of our exceptional team and the remarkable pupils we have the privilege to educate at Milbourne Lodge.
INSPECTION REPORTS 2025
Our Latest ISI Inspection
We are delighted to share a summary of our most recent inspection by the Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI), which took place in June 2025 under the new national inspection framework. While schools are no longer graded in the same way, we were pleased to meet all required standards and to receive highly positive feedback across all aspects of school life, from the quality of our teaching and leadership, to the strength of our pastoral care and relationships within the community. Our summary highlights the key takeaways from the full report and shows how Milbourne Lodge continues to deliver a truly rounded, ambitious, and values-led education for every child.

We especially warmly welcome our newest members of the Milbourne community who are joining us for the very first time.Welcome to the family Class Reception! Let the adventures begin. 🤗
🌿 Four values. One community.At Milbourne Lodge, we believe education is about so much more than what happens in the classroom. It’s about helping every child grow into a confident, caring and curious individual — ready to make a difference in the world around them.Community. Courage. Compassion. Creativity.Four values that guide us every day. ✨✨Compassion✨Our school is more than just a place of learning; it is a community where compassion flourishes. We look after, support and encourage each other to always be our best. Our school is a positive, safe and caring community in which all individuals are valued and respected, and enabled to develop their skills, talents and interests to the full; intellectually, physically and spiritually. We strive for the highest standards in pastoral care.✨Courage✨We encourage our pupils to face challenges head-on, to question, to explore, and to embrace the unknown with an open mind. Wraparound Care
Flexible and supportive care
At Milbourne Lodge, we understand the importance of providing flexible and supportive care around the school day to accommodate the needs of our families. Our comprehensive Wraparound Care programme is designed to offer a nurturing environment for children, ensuring they start and end their day in a positive and enriching setting.
From our Early Bird Group for the youngest learners to tailored Breakfast Clubs, Homework Groups, and structured After School Groups, we ensure every child is cared for, engaged, and prepared for the day ahead or given the perfect wind-down after a busy school day.
8am to 8.30am each morning This is available to children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2. The children are supervised in a Pre-Prep classroom by a member of the Pre-Prep staff until 8.30am when they are taken to their classroom.
It is expected that the children will have had breakfast before they arrive at school.
7.45am to 8.15am each morning in the school hall The children are supervised and given a healthy, wholesome breakfast. At 8.15am the Prep children will go to their classrooms and any Pre-Prep children will be taken to join the Early Bird Group.
Breakfast will be served from 7.45am – 7.55am; pupils need to be dropped off between these times in order to enjoy breakfast.
4pm to 5.05pm This is available to children in Years 3 to 5. Children are given a drink and a snack and then are encouraged to do their homework or read.
They are supervised by a member of staff until the bell goes at 5.05pm. Children must be signed up for Homework Group in advance and for specific days e.g. every Monday and Wednesday.
Group 1 – 3.30pm to 4pm | Group 2 – 4pm to 5.05pm These are supervised after school groups available to children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2. One session runs from 3.30pm to 4pm each afternoon, and the other from 3.30pm to 5.05pm.
The children will be given a healthy snack at each session.

Scholarships and Results
Empowering minds, inspiring futures
Since the 1950s Milbourne Lodge has been renowned for its academic excellence. Helping our pupils believe in themselves and furnishing them with the tools to grasp every academic challenge is what motivates everyone here. We are known as one of the pre-eminent Prep schools because the whole experience is underpinned by gently encouraging each child to take every opportunity and to always search for more.
2025 11+ Results and Scholarships
2025 13+ Results and Scholarships
Early Years Foundation Stage - GLD Data
Reception
At the end of the academic year 2022/2023, an exceptional 92% of Reception students (children aged 4-5) at Milbourne Lodge attained a Good Level of Development (GLD), significantly more than the national average of 69%. Additionally, a remarkable 15% of these students exceeded to GLD, showcasing excellence across all 17 Early Learning Goals (ELGs).
Children are defined as having reached a good level of development at the end of the EYFS if they have attained at least the expected level in:
The early learning goals in the prime areas of learning (personal, social and emotional development; physical development; and communication and language) and
The early learning goals in the specific areas of mathematics and literacy
Maths and English Scores
Mean SAS (Standard age score)
Our pupils' academic progress is carefully monitored through annual National Standardised tests in English and Mathematics. The Progress Test in English (PTE) assessed pupils' technical English skills, including spelling, grammar, punctuation and reading comprehension. The Progress Test in Maths (PTM) monitors their mathematical skills and knowledge in areas such as number, shape, data handling and algebra, as well as their mathematical reasoning and problem-solving abilities.
The results presented above show age-standardised scored at Milbourne Lodge. Notably, our pupils have consistently achieved scores significantly above the national average in both English and Maths. The SAS is a students raw score converted into a score that takes into account the student's precise age (in years and months) and benchmarks it to a national database. The average score is always 100.

Music
Nurturing skills and confidence through music
Music is seen as an integral part of the curriculum at Milbourne Lodge. Learning to play and appreciate music can encourage participation, teamwork, and a sense of group identity as well as increasing creativity. Music develops the children’s ability to understand themselves and relate to others, thus promoting self-confidence and social skills. It can also support learning in other subject areas. The ability to listen and concentrate and the facility for self-expression are useful life skills.
A comprehensive approach to music education
The teaching of music in class is primarily aimed at developing the children’s understanding and appreciation of the subject. Pupils’ natural musicianship skills are developed and honed through singing and aural work (to develop musical memory, the inner ear and a true sense of pitch), use of classroom percussion (to develop a sense of rhythm and pulse) and through exploring the four main pillars of the music curriculum: performing, composing, listening and appraising. All pupils are taught to sing and to play tuned and un-tuned percussion and are introduced to the basics of music theory in class. They also undertake a comprehensive project on ‘The Orchestra’ in class. Many of them then go on to take up an orchestral instrument as a result.
Diverse instrumental tuition
We have a team of peripatetic music staff who offer tuition on a range of instruments including: flute, saxophone, clarinet, guitar, oboe, violin, cello, trumpet, piano, percussion and recorder. Individual theory of music and singing lessons are also available. Lessons are mostly during the lunch-hour, games time or after school. All pupils learning an instrument have the chance to perform in various school music ensembles such as the Concert Band and String Ensemble.
Unleashing creativity
Apart from instrumental tuition at Milbourne we offer fun and innovative after-school extra-curricular activities in the field of Music Technology. M:Tech is a creative composition course in which children create exciting music using the latest music technologies. The course is available to children age 7 – 13 in the Prep and is suitable for all levels of musical ability.
There are many opportunities to get involved with Music at Milbourne:
Concert Band and String Ensemble
Musical achievement
There are musical events each term, including the Carol Concert in the Autumn Term, the Spring Term Showcase Concert and the Year 7 and 8 musical at Esher Theatre in the Summer Term. The musical ensembles and individual instrumentalists also perform at the Dickensian Evening and the Summer Show. The school also has a thriving choral department and pupils are encouraged to join either the Junior or Senior choir. These choirs participate in various concerts and events, to which all parents are welcome. Children with outstanding musical talent have the opportunity to try for Music Scholarships and numerous music awards have been won to many of the major independent senior schools.

Art &IT
Teaching Art & IT in a unique and holistic way
At Milbourne Lodge we believe that Art & IT are essential elements of a balanced and rounded education. By working with an ambitious and rich curriculum, that is grounded in wellbeing, we set aspirational creative targets. Combining the strength of both subjects our pupils achieve outstanding results. We are committed to helping our girls and boys experience, value and enjoy these lessons as a means of communication and creative expression.
Voice of the Parent survey 2024
Our projects
Combining our strengths in Art & IT
We have developed a unique way of inspiring our pupils. Living in a world that is constantly changing we strive to embrace these innovations. Although our lessons are taught separately, we plan and work closely together to deliver joint outcomes. A new theme is chosen each year, deliberately very different from the last. Examples include ‘It’s a Wild World’, ‘Shoes’, ‘Sport’, ‘Money Can’t Buy’, ‘Numbers’, ‘The Secret Garden’ and ‘Portmeirion’. A strong emphasis on wellbeing is nurtured in both our departments. We have recently developed and built our own Outdoor Learning Area at Milbourne Lodge which allows us to focus strongly on nature and the benefits of learning outside.
Celebrating Success and Community links
To showcase pupils work, we enter national competitions and have had considerable success. Milbourne’s Art & IT have been exhibited at The Royal College of Art, The National Gallery, The Saatchi Gallery, The Northampton Museum of Shoes, The Natural History Museum, The Houses of Parliament, RHS Wisley, The British Film Institute (BFI) and Edinburgh Film Festival. We enjoy the opportunity to work with our local community. The best way to experience our unique projects is to visit our departments during one of our termly Open Days or follow us on social media.
Portmeirion 2023
This project was inspired by the enchanting and colourful Italianate style village on the coast of North Wales. Pupils spent a year learning to ‘cherish the past, adorn the present and construct for the future’ in the words of Sir Clough Williams-Ellis, the uniquely eccentric architect of Portmeirion.
Our Numbers theme took Prep school pupils (Year 3 to Year 8) on a wonderful journey of exploration.
Our final Art & IT projects reflect the depth of research and learning achieved.
The Secret Garden 2021
Based on the life and times of Frances Hodgson Burnett pupils began this project by reading the story of ‘The Secret Garden’ before enjoying a red-carpet screening of the 1993 version of the film. Both proved inspirational when we once again found ourselves in Lockdown during Spring term. With the arrival of the Summer term came a welcome return to classrooms and pupils then enjoyed creating their own Secret Garden as well as working together on film and animation projects.

Prep
A love of learning
Milbourne Lodge School prioritises a robust preparatory program to prepare pupils comprehensively for their academic journey and beyond. Rooted in a nurturing environment, the school focuses on building a strong foundation for academic success, character development, and social skills. The curriculum aims to instil a love for learning and equip pupils with essential skills, fostering a supportive community that prepares them both academically and emotionally for future challenges.

Years 3 & 4
Ages 7 to 9
Children enter the Prep school in Year 3 and the year group comprises two parallel classes. Both classes will be taught the majority of their lessons by their respective Form Tutor but will have specialist teachers for French, Science, Art, IT and Music. This gives pupils the security of working with their Form Tutor alongside opportunities to develop and branch out under the guidance of others. In Year 4, the year group is introduced to specialist subjects such as Latin. Pupils can then begin to fine-tune their interests.
Years 5 & 6
Ages 9 to 11
Pre-Testing for entry to Senior Schools takes place in the Autumn Term of Year 6. Pupils are therefore prepared from Year 5 for the various requirements for this. Pupils receive designated lessons that focus on Verbal and Non-Verbal Reasoning, along with significant preparation for the different styles of interview which they will inevitably face. It is our aim in these crucial years to ensure our pupils feel confident and ready for the rigours of Pre-Testing. However, this does not take away from the curriculum’s breadth and depth. Our pupils have many opportunities to express themselves in Art, IT, Music, Sport and during Extra-Curricular activities such as Debate Club, Chatterbooks and Drama Club.
By Year 6 pupils’ personalities have truly begun to flourish. The more they engage with one another, the better their fluency, articulation and communication skills become. This is testimony to the work, experience, skill and encouragement of the academic staff. Throughout these two years they face a diverse set of challenges. Ancient Greek is also introduced to the curriculum in Year 6.
Years 7 & 8
Ages 11 to 13
The curriculum for the final two years in the Prep School is planned around preparing pupils for the rigours of Senior School life and preparing some for Scholarship examinations. All our boys and girls attain the highest academic standards required to enter the best Independent Senior Schools in the country and they move smoothly from Milbourne to the next stage of their education. We know that our children really thrive on the opportunities and the possibilities opened up to them as they explore, connect and develop on a rich diet of academic stimulus and regular outdoor activities. Critical Thinking, Drama and Spanish are introduced in Years 7 & 8 and pupils have the opportunity to take part in a wide range of field studies and trips.

Foundations for early learning
The teaching in our Reception class is based on the Early Years Foundation Stage Framework. This stage is the period of education up to the age of 5 years. Our Reception comprises two parallel classes.
Curriculum
The curriculum considers and incorporates the following seven areas of learning:
Our goal is to enhance this core curriculum by providing challenging, fun opportunities for learning, while maintaining a strong emphasis on acquiring the basic tools vital to early schooling. We always remember that every day is an adventure and a time of discovery. However, we carefully structure the work to help children develop their skills and relationships. This enables them to reach their Early Learning Goals by the end of the Reception year. In fact most of our children exceed them.

Tailored learning and continuous assessment
We also recognise that all children develop and learn in different ways and at different speeds. It is therefore important to differentiate accordingly. This allows all our children to achieve and progress within an enabling environment that caters for their individual needs. By observing the children at both work and play we are able to continuously assess progress and attainment. We maintain a profile of each child’s development during their Reception year. This profile is shared with parents and staff at the end of Reception before each child moves into Year 1.

Years 1 & 2
Fostering essential skills and values
In Year 1, the curriculum underscores the significant learning which needs to take place. Teaching and learning opportunities encourage active engagement, motivation and depth of learning. Quality experiences also help develop the right attributes and capabilities that are so important to our pupils throughout their school life.
Foundations for future success
We build on the enjoyment and enthusiasm for learning fostered in Reception. Our curriculum draws on the best elements of traditional teaching, with a strong emphasis on literacy and numeracy. It is strongly supported by a broad range of subjects and activities designed to widen horizons and develop children’s imaginations. Subject areas include History, Geography, Science, French, RE, Art, Design and Technology and Computing. Confidence, personality and core numeracy and literacy skills are fully developed in Year 2, so that they are ready to move into the Prep school.
A seamless transition to Year 3
In Year 2, fundamental aspects of learning are in place. Now the process of building further can begin. The curriculum is designed to constantly engage and challenge pupils. At this stage, teaching and learning further promotes confidence and independence alongside positive attitudes and dispositions. By the end of Year 2 your child will have received a thorough academic grounding of the highest standard. At this point they will be ready to build on this foundation as they move into Year 3 in the Prep school.

An Education With Purpose.For a Life of Possibilities
We know that children learn best when they are happy and engaged. Our schools are vibrant communities built on friendship and kindness. Imagination and playfulness are woven into school life and our diverse curriculum enables pupils to explore new experiences and discover new passions. Education is a precious and exhilarating journey of self-discovery, and we want pupils to thrive socially and emotionally, as well as academically.
We’re here to inspire a lifelong love of learning in every pupil. Through our rich curriculum and highly individualised teaching, we help them develop genuine intellectual curiosity and academic confidence. With life skills embedded into every lesson, pupils are challenged and inspired to think deeply and critically, solve problems and communicate effectively – a solid foundation for their lives ahead.
Nurturing Their Extraordinary
Our classrooms are creative and stimulating places in which to learn. We celebrate effort, welcome debate and see mistakes as part of the journey to improvement. Pupils are encouraged to aim high, rise to the challenge and take pride in their achievements. At the same time, they learn the lifelong value of collaboration, empathy and mutual respect, crucial qualities that will stand them in good stead.
LIFE-READY LEARNERS
The future is complex and fast-changing. Young people need future-ready skills, in addition to strong academic achievement. A successful and fulfilling adulthood is built on a well-rounded education, imbued with moral values, sound judgement and self-discipline grounded in self-worth. A Blenheim education equips them with all of these qualities and many more.
The future is theirs to embrace and the possibilities are endless. Together, let’s make sure they’re ready for it.
